previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with shortness of breath, confusion, and a week of productive cough after returning from travel. He rapidly decompensated, requiring intubation for hypoxic respiratory failure. He was diagnosed with parainfluenza virus and Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteremia, leading to severe sepsis, acute kidney injury, rhabdomyolysis, and metabolic encephalopathy. He was treated with a 21-day course of IV ceftriaxone, supportive care, and management of complications including acute urinary retention and transaminitis. His condition gradually improved, with resolution of infection, renal recovery, and return of mental clarity. He was extubated, transitioned to oral intake, and regained mobility. He was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with plans to resume myeloma and latent TB treatment after outpatient follow-up.
